page_title: Depflush – free Mac cleaner for developers

summary.name: Depflush
summary.one_liner: Depflush is a free, open-source macOS cleaner that finds disk space left behind by developer tools such as Docker images, stale node_modules and vendor folders, SQL dump duplicates, old IDE caches, and duplicate photos and videos.
use_cases: Reclaim gigabytes taken by Docker images and build cache
Remove node_modules and vendor folders from projects not touched in a year
Find and remove duplicate SQL dumps across project folders
Clear caches from old JetBrains and other IDE versions
Remove duplicate photos and videos in Downloads, Desktop and Pictures
Free disk space on a developer Mac
summary.what_it_does: Depflush scans a Mac for developer leftovers: Docker build cache and unused images, vendor and node_modules folders in dormant projects, duplicate SQL dumps over 100 MB (compared by size then SHA-256), and caches from more than 30 locations including older JetBrains versions. It also finds byte-for-byte duplicate photos and videos in Pictures, Movies, Documents, Desktop and Downloads, keeping one original. Items are shown with path and size, and the user confirms the total before anything is removed. Files go to the Trash by default.
notable: Open source under GPL-3.0, source on GitHub
Never preselects Docker containers, volumes or locally built images; they are shown with a warning
Byte-for-byte duplicate detection that only removes copies while the original remains
No account, analytics or network calls; scan runs locally
caveats: App is not yet notarized by Apple, so first launch requires approving it in System Settings > Privacy & Security
Full Disk Access is optional and needed to size Mail and iPhone backups
Support is via voluntary donations; the page states Apple's developer fee of 99 euro per year is the reason for donations
